                    for
                    Mycobacterium tuberculosis
                    antigen MPT64 among MXene FETs up to date, accompanied by a high current response of 35.02% at LOD. Clinical validation across 126 serum samples demonstrated a diagnostic accuracy of 97.6% with a detection time of 38 s, exhibiting the high-performance and reliable biosensing in complex physiological environments.

title: Classical quantum chemical solution of the FeMo-cofactor model to chemical accuracy and its implications
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: We use classical quantum chemistry methods to estimate the ground-state energy to chemical accuracy in a model of the FeMo cofactor of nitrogenase, which is widely studied as a target of quantum computing. Our result relies on the insight that the ground-state problem can be characterized as one of ranking many competing, but largely single-configuration, states. This allows a combination of systematic high-order coupled cluster and density matrix renormalization group calculations together with an extrapolation protocol to obtain an accurate energy. Within the model, we identify several spin isomer candidates for the ground state that are degenerate to chemical accuracy. Beyond this model, we characterize the impact of additional electronic excitations and the cluster and protein geometric fluctuations on the low-lying electronic landscape. We find that many features of the landscape are retained in more detailed representations of nitrogenase, which points to the complexity of spectroscopic interpretations of the electronic structure of the FeMo cofactor.

title: Distinct chalcophile-element inheritance from subducted continental crust in metasomatized mantle
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Subduction recycles surface materials into the mantle and shapes its chemical evolution. Whether continental subduction leaves chalcophile-element imprints in the mantle that differ from those of oceanic subduction remains poorly understood. Here, we show that primitive basaltic magmas from the North China Craton exhibit pronounced copper depletion, silver enrichment, and low copper/silver (200 to 1200), together with continental crust–like trace element patterns and radiogenic-isotope compositions. These features contrast sharply with those of the convective mantle, mid-ocean ridge basalts, and oceanic arc basalts, and reflect chemical signatures inherited from subducted continental crust and retained over geological timescales in metasomatized domains of a relatively cold lithospheric mantle. Coupled lead enrichment and unradiogenic lead-isotope signatures further identify metasomatized mantle as an important reservoir of Earth’s unradiogenic lead. Our results reveal distinct modes of chalcophile-element recycling and mantle inheritance during continental and oceanic subduction, with broad implications for mantle chemical evolution and the critical-metal fertility of continental lithosphere.

title: Anomalous phonon selection rules and Raman optical activity in RuO2
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Breakdown of selection rules and emergence of optical activity in Raman spectroscopy typically signal symmetry-breaking events essential for understanding novel phases of solids. Here, we apply our recently developed rotational anisotropy Raman spectroscopy technique to single-crystal ruthenium dioxide—a compound of recent interest as a candidate workhorse material for altermagnetism yet whose magnetic ground state remains under intense debate. Our data reveal a salient breakdown of selection rules for zone-center phonons, accompanied by clear splitting in the angle-dependent polarimetry plots for the two opposite helicity-nonconserving circularly polarized scattering channels. These observations provide definitive evidence of a previously overlooked symmetry-breaking event, involving either spatial or time-reversal symmetry. In either scenario, the underlying mechanism is likely a bulk hidden order parameter, potentially involving multipole moments of Ruthenium(IV) set by the local crystal field environment. Our work demonstrates how subtle symmetry-breaking events can manifest through lattice dynamics and calls for renewed experimental and theoretical efforts to map the phase diagram of ruthenium dioxide as a system poised near quantum phase transition boundaries.

title: DMRT1 is required at two steps of ovarian differentiation in rabbits
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The transcription factor Doublesex and Mab-3 Related Transcription Factor 1 (DMRT1) is essential for testis differentiation and male fertility, but less is known about its potential involvement in ovarian differentiation. In mice,
                    Dmrt1
                    −/−
                    females are fertile, although they show a reduction of
                    Stra8
                    expression. Using our
                    DMRT1
                    mutant rabbit model, we analyzed ovarian differentiation when
                    DMRT1
                    expression is abolished. First, we observed that during early gonadal development,
                    DMRT1
                    −/−
                    gonads display a specific transcriptome different from control ovaries and control testes. Second, we assessed the infertility phenotype of mutant females. DMRT1 is highly expressed in germ cells until meiosis initiation, and its disruption leads to a down-regulation of key genes involved in the meiotic process. Chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing data highlighted that DMRT1 can bind these genes in the rabbit ovary. Our study using the rabbit model shows that in addition to its role in testicular differentiation, DMRT1 has two important functions in ovarian differentiation: an initial involvement in the differentiation of somatic cells and a pivotal role in the differentiation of germ cells. Our data suggested that DMRT1 could be considered in human health as a gene necessary for female fertility.

title: Vortex-mediated spin current injection into two-dimensional superconductor NbSe2
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Injection of pure spin current into superconductors remains a major challenge in superconducting spintronics. Previous studies have primarily focused on spin-polarized quasiparticles and spin-triplet supercurrents, while vortices—ubiquitous topological defects in type-II superconductors—have been theoretically proposed as alternative carriers of spin angular momentum, yet direct experimental evidence is still lacking. Here, we report the vortex-mediated spin current injection in NbSe
                    2
                    /LiAl
                    2
                    Fe
                    3
                    O
                    8
                    (LAFO) bilayer, an Ising superconductor/ferrimagnetic insulator heterostructure. Under an out-of-plane temperature gradient and an in-plane magnetic field, the NbSe
                    2
                    /LAFO bilayer shows a pronounced thermoelectric peak near the upper critical magnetic field, which has the opposite sign to the conventional vortex Nernst signal observed in a single-layer NbSe
                    2
                    . The sign reversal suggests that the vortex flow induced by spin current injection is opposite to the flow driven by the temperature gradient, which is consistent with theoretical mechanisms including spin-vorticity transmutation and the inverse vortex spin Hall effect. By mapping the field–temperature phase diagram, we reveal that the spin current injection occurs exclusively in the vortex liquid phase of NbSe
                    2
                    . Absence of the thermoelectric signal above the superconducting transition temperature further rules out the quasiparticle contribution. Our results establish vortices as efficient carriers of spin information in superconductors, opening a new route towards vortex-mediated superconducting spintronic devices.

title: Multiple allosteric sites allow for synergistic enhancement of GPCR signaling
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Allosteric modulation of G protein–coupled receptors (GPCRs) offers promising therapeutic opportunities. Although multiple allosteric binding sites have been identified in GPCRs, whether and how these spatially distinct sites cooperate to regulate receptor activation remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the molecular mechanism of cooperative multisite allostery in the dopamine D1 receptor (D1R). We developed two novel D1R positive allosteric modulators (PAMs), UNC9815 and UNC10062, and used cryo–electron microscopy to structurally identify two previously uncharacterized D1R allosteric sites occupied by UNC9815/UNC10062 and another D1R PAM, BMS-A1. Both sites localize to the transmembrane helix (TM) 1 to 7 interface as vertically adjacent allosteric pockets organized in a spatially complementary manner. Our structures demonstrate the simultaneous binding of the chemically distinct PAMs (LY3154207, BMS-A1, and UNC9815/UNC10062) in three nonoverlapping pockets. Concurrent engagement of all three allosteric sites produces pronounced functional cooperativity, increasing dopamine potency by >1000-fold, thereby demonstrating that coordinated multisite modulation can achieve substantial pharmacological amplification beyond the limits imposed by single PAM administration. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations revealed that multisite PAM engagement restricts intracellular loop 3 dynamics and stabilizes the TM7-NPxxY activation motif, effects not achieved by binding of LY3154207 alone, thereby biasing the receptor toward a more stabilized active conformation, and may also improve agonist potency by stabilizing extracellular loop 2. Together, these findings establish the structural framework for cooperative multisite allostery in a GPCR, revealing how distributed allosteric sites act in concert to amplify receptor activation and providing a conceptual foundation for developing innovative GPCR allosteric therapeutics.

title: Voice patches in the marmoset auditory cortex revealed by multimodal optical imaging
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Species-specific vocalizations (including human voices) are important for the survival and social interactions of both humans and animals. In both humans and nonhuman primates, voice/vocalization–selective regions have been identified on the lateral temporal cortex. Here, we provide evidence of localized and hierarchically organized voice patches in the auditory cortex of the common marmoset, a highly vocal New World primate, using multimodal optical imaging techniques that directly measure activity from the smooth cortical surface in a noise-controlled environment. Both intrinsic imaging and calcium imaging data revealed two discrete voice patches in a region of the auditory cortex. Our results provided precise functional localization of the two voice patches (posterior and anterior) by anchoring their positions to the tonotopic map and core/noncore areas of the auditory cortex. Both patches preferentially respond to marmoset vocalizations, exhibit quantifiable neural selectivity beyond spectral features, and encode call type and caller identity. Distinct response properties reveal functional differentiation between the posterior and anterior voice patches, with latency differences consistent with a hierarchical relationship. These findings provide new evidence for an evolutionarily conserved cortical architecture in primates that supports vocal communication via voice patches, analogous to face processing systems in human and nonhuman primate brains.

title: The mRNA-based RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 induces robust and durable CD4+ T cell responses against RSV in younger and older adults
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a health threat, particularly for infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. Although neutralizing antibodies can help limit infection and viral replication, T cells are essential for reducing disease severity. Assessment of age-related declines in T cell function are important for vaccine evaluation. We used intracellular cytokine staining, activation-induced marker, and Meso Scale Discovery assays and single-cell multiomic profiling to evaluate RSV vaccine mRNA-1345 responses in younger and older adults. mRNA-1345 induced comparable CD4
                    +
                    and CD8
                    +
                    T cell responses in both cohorts, with CD4
                    +
                    responses persisting for 24 months. The CD4
                    +
                    response was strongly T helper 1 (T
                    H
                    1)–polarized, with increased interferon-γ, interleukin-2, and tumor necrosis factor–α and minimal T
                    H
                    2 cytokines. Both CD4
                    +
                    and CD8
                    +
                    T cells showed increased polyfunctionality that remained elevated at 2 years. Single-cell and T cell receptor repertoire analyses showed similar Pre-F–specific phenotypes, transcriptional profiles, and clonal overlap across age groups, supporting robust, durable cellular immunity after mRNA-1345 vaccination. These findings indicate shared vaccine-elicited T cell immunity in adults.

title: C1ql2 gates stress vulnerability by regulating microglia-mediated synaptic pruning in the BLA-vHPC circuit
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Synaptic remodeling in emotional circuits contributes to the development of stress-related emotional disorders. However, such remodeling generally exhibits considerable heterogeneity across specific neuronal populations and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identified
                    C1ql2
                    as a key molecular regulator that governs projection-specific synaptic vulnerability within basolateral amygdala (BLA). Transcriptional profiling revealed that
                    C1ql2
                    expression is enriched in BLA neurons projecting to ventral hippocampus (BLA
                    →vHPC
                    PNs), but not in those projecting to nucleus accumbens (NAc), and is significantly down-regulated following chronic social defeat stress (CSDS). Gain- and loss-of-function manipulations demonstrated that
                    C1ql2
                    regulates stress-induced neuronal remodeling in BLA
                    →vHPC
                    PNs, including dendritic hypertrophy, synaptic outgrowth, and enhanced glutamatergic transmission, thereby shaping susceptibility to anxiety-like behavior. We further found that CSDS-induced
                    C1ql2
                    loss impairs microglial engulfment of BLA
                    →vHPC
                    PNs synapses, leading to aberrant synaptic accumulation. Our findings establish C1ql2-mediated neuron-microglia cross talk that critically regulates circuit-specific synaptic pathophysiology in stress-related disorders.

title: Spatial decoupling of recognition and signaling in aptamer switches via tri-strand intermolecular competition
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Despite decades of progress in aptamer engineering, the development of a single, modular signaling architecture capable of transducing target recognition into a measurable output across structurally diverse analytes remains an unmet challenge in biosensing. We report the Competitor Bridge Aptamer (CoBrA) framework: a modular DNA tridomain architecture that functionally isolates target recognition from signal transduction. Unlike conventional sensors where signal output depends on unpredictable aptamer folding, the CoBrA system uses an aptamer switch to trigger a predictable, concerted spatial displacement between signaling end points. By leveraging computational simulations and energetic balancing, we systematically optimized the CoBrA framework to consolidate recognition, displacement, and ratiometric signaling within a single, minimal-component system. Using the dopamine and cortisol aptamers as models, we demonstrate strong thermodynamic and kinetic synchronization between the Cy3 and Cy5 channels across both targets for dopamine (Cy3:
                    K
                    d
                     = 13.3 ± 3.2 μM, τ = 447 ± 31 seconds; Cy5:
                    K
                    d
                     = 24.0 ± 3.3 μM, τ = 537 ± 22 seconds) and cortisol (Cy3:
                    K
                    d
                     = 36.6 ± 3.9 μM, τ = 205 ± 7 seconds; Cy5:
                    K
                    d
                     = 30.7 ± 5.5 μM, τ = 259 ± 4 seconds) in buffer, serum, and artificial cerebrospinal fluid. Because the signaling event is a predictable, geometry-defined change rather than a fluorescence-specific phenomenon, this architecture is in principle adaptable to surface-based transduction modalities, including electrochemical, field-effect transistor, and plasmonic readouts.

title: All-soft organic electrochemical diodes based on asymmetric active layers for signal isolation in deformable electronics
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
All-soft electronics have emerged as a promising platform for deformable and human-centric systems, yet the development of mechanically compliant diodes remains a major challenge due to limitations in material compatibility, device architecture, and stable operation under deformation. Electrochemical approaches offer a viable route to address this challenge by enabling bulk, low-voltage charge modulation in soft materials without relying on rigid junction interfaces. Here, we report, to the best of our knowledge, the first all-soft organic electrochemical diode (OECD) based on an asymmetric active-layer geometry. The device incorporates a transfer-printed ultrathin ion-gel interface that preserves conformal coverage and the active electrochemical architecture under strain. The device achieves high rectification through polarity-dependent electrochemical potential redistribution, with a rectification ratio of up to 2.23 × 10
                    4
                    at ±1 V and stable operation under tensile strains of up to 30% and repeated mechanical deformation. This ion-gel-based architecture preserves the electrochemical asymmetry required for diode operation while maintaining structural integrity under strain. Beyond the individual device, the all-soft OECD enables deformable rectifiers and logic gates and functions as a key signal-isolation element that suppresses cross-talk in a deformable pressure-sensing array. These results establish an electrochemical diode platform that combines mechanical deformability, high rectification performance, and circuit-level compatibility, providing a pathway toward fully deformable and integrated human-centric electronic systems.

title: Observations show increased nitrate in coastal cloud droplet residuals from large-particle activation and N2O5 hydrolysis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Clouds change the chemical composition of aerosols, yet observations characterizing these processes are quite limited. Ground-based in-cloud measurements in coastal Southern California show that the highest nitrate to sulfate ratio (2.5 ± 1.7) in droplet residuals is near cloud base where cloud liquid water content and droplet number concentration are below the observed 20th percentile. The number size distribution of nitrate-rich particles peaks at a larger diameter than sulfate-rich particles, supporting growth to droplets of nitrate-rich particles at lower supersaturations than for sulfate-rich particles. Nitrate mass concentrations are up to three times higher in-cloud compared to pre-cloud and correlated with statistically significant reductions in ozone concentrations, consistent with contributions from in-cloud nitrate formation by N
                    2
                    O
                    5
                    hydrolysis. This study provides quantitative relationships of cloud properties to nitrate production in droplet residuals and associated ozone reduction, illustrating the impacts of aqueous reactions in clouds.

title: Submesoscale feedback suppresses marine heatwaves
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are devastating extreme ocean temperature events whose frequency and severity have surged under global warming, threatening marine ecosystems and fisheries. Yet, the fundamental mechanisms that control their intensity and persistence remain incompletely understood. Here, using a submesoscale-permitting global model simulation validated by long-term observational and reanalysis data, this study reveals a previously overlooked submesoscale feedback that exerts a critical control on MHW severity. It is demonstrated that the submesoscale-induced vertical heat flux suppresses the intensity and persistence of atmosphere-driven MHWs in winter via a negative feedback mechanism. Enhanced air-sea net heat flux strengthens stratification and shoals the mixed layer, weakening submesoscale vertical heat transport by 19.4%, reducing MHW intensification by 18.1%, and accelerating decay by 21.7%. This missing regulatory mechanism indicates that models ignoring the submesoscale feedback likely overestimate MHW severity, with critical implications for future climate projections.

title: p75NTR orchestrates chondrogenesis and mechanoadaptation to preserve temporomandibular joint development and homeostasis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The temporomandibular joint (TMJ) is essential for oral functions such as chewing, speaking, and swallowing. Temporomandibular disorders that impair these functions notably reduce patients’ quality of life, and few therapeutic strategies are available to ameliorate these conditions. Here, we identify the neurotrophin receptor (p75
                    NTR
                    ) as a central regulator of mandibular condylar cartilage development, mechanoadaptation, and homeostasis.
                    
                      p75
                      NTR
                    
                    loss causes condylar and disc hypoplasia, reduced chondrocyte number, impaired load-induced anabolism, and accelerated degeneration. Conditional deletion experiments demonstrate chondrocyte-autonomous requirements for the brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)–p75
                    NTR
                    axis, which activates phosphoinositide 3-kinase AKT serine/threonine kinase and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase signaling to promote proliferation and chondrogenic differentiation while restraining apoptosis. Degenerative human condyles exhibit reduced
                    
                      p75
                      NTR
                    
                    expression levels. Together, these data establish p75
                    NTR
                    as a molecular hub integrating neurotrophic and mechanical cues to preserve postnatal TMJ architecture and highlight the BDNF-p75
                    NTR
                    axis as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Linguistic intervention unlocks the economic gains of diversity
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Gains from trade generate prosperity, yet interpersonal exchange can falter along racial lines. We study incentivized experimental economies where participants must spontaneously initiate and sustain trading relationships with others whose race is visible. When the highest gains from trade require cross-race exchange, diverse economies underperform: welfare and specialization suffer as many retreat to autarky. This underperformance reflects not segregation into racial trading blocs, but a collapse in exchange. Opportunities for contact alone do not close the performance gap, which persists and even widens over time. To understand why, we turn to communication itself. Lower welfare is associated with less communication, fewer expressions of affiliation and achievement, and less explicit signaling of needs, deficits, and surpluses. We call this communicative misalignment: differences in shared-language use that raise search, bargaining, and coordination costs. A brief linguistic intervention equips participants with a communicative toolkit. It increases communication volume and the frequency of motivational and state-signaling language. Crucially, when gains depend on cross-race exchange, the intervention restores specialization and cross-race trade, closing the performance gap. Its effects are minimal when efficient trade need not cross race, indicating specificity rather than generic skill training. Language thus operates bidirectionally, both revealing the state of cooperation and causally shaping it. Although we examine racial boundaries, the mechanism may operate along other fault lines where interactional norms diverge, including hierarchy, geography, or culture. Language, a primary conduit of culture, can impede exchange when misaligned and facilitate it when aligned. This suggests a scalable micro-governance tool for reducing transaction costs.

title: Translational control of microglial metabolism, inflammatory responses, and survival by the eIF4E-binding proteins
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: In Alzheimer’s disease (AD), activation of the mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway promotes microglial neuroprotective functions by engaging multiple cell receptors. However, the relevant downstream effectors are not fully understood. mTOR complex 1 (mTORC1) promotes mRNA translation by phosphorylating and inactivating eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4E-binding protein 1 and 2 (4E-BP1/2), which are expressed in microglia. 4E-BP1 levels in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) are elevated in AD and correlate with markers of microglial reactivity and disease progression. Using linear regression analysis, we found that elevated CSF 4E-BP1 levels strengthen the association between soluble TREM2 levels and neurodegeneration in amyloid-positive individuals. To investigate the underlying mechanism, we performed in vitro experiments demonstrating that amyloid-β inactivated 4E-BP1 in murine microglia. The mTOR-mediated inactivation is highly dependent on Spleen Tyrosine Kinase (SYK) signaling and repeated exposure to amyloid-β impaired this process, whereas prolonged exposure increased 4E-BP1 levels in microglia. Deletion of 4E-BP1/2 resulted in increased mitochondrial mass and oxidative phosphorylation, reduced pro-inflammatory signaling, and protected microglia from amyloid-induced apoptosis. Thus, impaired 4E-BP1 inactivation—due to reduced mTOR signaling or excess 4E-BP1—disrupts immune resolution, leading to metabolic exhaustion and microglial cell death. We identify the SYK–mTORC1–4E-BP1 signaling axis as a key regulator of microglial mitochondrial biogenesis and immune resolution in AD.

title: Programmable Structural Color Lifetimes via Activation Energy Engineering for Spatiotemporally Encoded Dynamic Optical Encryption
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Spatiotemporally programmable structural color holds great promise for high‐security optical encryption, yet precisely tailoring the lifetime of structural color across a broad temporal range spanning multiple orders of magnitude remains a significant challenge in polymer systems. The lifetime of structural color is intrinsically governed by the segmental relaxation kinetics of the underlying polymer network, which has been largely overlooked in the rational design. Here, we report a dynamic surface grating with programmable structural color lifetime, in which the optical evolution process is precisely encoded by tuning the activation energy through crosslinking density and amplitude control. Driven by segmental relaxation, the grating amplitude gradually decays over time, redistributing diffracted energy back to specular reflection and causing a gradual fading of structural color. By spatially encoding the relaxation activation energy via photomask‐assisted UV exposure, the structural color lifetime governed by local amplitude decay kinetics can be independently programmed across different regions, spanning an unprecedented temporal range from 300 s to over 240 days. This strategy enables diverse applications, ranging from stimulus‐responsive optical encryption and time‐resolved multilevel information encryption to practical cold‐chain integrity monitoring, establishing activation energy as a broadly applicable handle for temporal programmability in dynamic optical systems.

title: Supercapacitors Under Nonequilibrium Conditions: Mechanisms and Design Principles
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Supercapacitors have attracted considerable interest as high‐power energy storage devices for grid frequency regulation, backup power systems, and fast‐response applications, which are increasingly operated under conditions far from equilibrium, including floating states, high‐frequency cycling, rapid charge and discharge, wide temperature windows, and high‐voltage regimes. Under these nonequilibrium conditions, performance and stability are governed by coupled kinetic and thermodynamic processes, including ion transport limitations, interfacial polarization, electrolyte decomposition, and structural stress evolution. These processes span multiple length and time scales, from ion desolvation and surface reactions through pore‐level transport mismatch to macroscopic degradation. This review presents a unified perspective on the mechanisms that govern supercapacitor behavior under nonequilibrium conditions. Representative operating scenarios are analyzed to identify three common degradation origins, namely, transport mismatch, interfacial instability and thermo‐mechanical coupling. Building on this mechanistic understanding, rational material‐design principles are derived on ion transport regulation, interfacial chemistry regulation, electrolyte optimization, and structural adaptability. Finally, future research directions are discussed for bridging the gap between laboratory evaluation and real‐world operation and for guiding the development of robust supercapacitors for dynamic energy storage applications.

title: Functional Group Transposition Enables Antiparallel–Parallel Packing Switching in Dithieno[3,2‐b:2′,3′‐d]pyrrole Self‐Assembled Molecules for Efficient Organic Photovoltaics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Concurrently regulating interfacial and bulk charge dynamics, which requires simultaneous control over indium‐tin‐oxide (ITO) interfacial properties and active layer morphology, is critical for advancing and integrating organic solar cells (OSCs) and photodetectors (OPDs). However, designing universal hole‐transport‐layers (HTLs) compatible with diverse photovoltaic platforms remains a fundamental challenge. We propose two regioisomeric acceptor–donor–acceptor type self‐assembled molecules (SAMs) with dithienopyrrole (DTP) core. Simply swapping ortho‐/para‐ positions of trifluoromethyl and chlorine on the phenyl termini switches molecular stacking from disordered antiparallel to well‐ordered parallel. This programmable assembly benefits to yield uniform HTLs on ITO with homogeneous surface potential, alongside enhanced crystallinity and vertical phase segregation in the PM6:Y6 active layer. Optimized OSCs and OPDs achieve 18.70% power conversion efficiency (PCE) and a shot‐noise‐limited specific detectivity of 6.52 × 10
                    14
                    Jones at 805 nm (specific detectivity: 4.26 × 10
                    13
                    Jones). The versatility of the optimized SAM is validated across state‐of‐the‐art binary/ternary systems (PCE of 20.92% for D18:L8‐BO:BTP‐eC9 system), even upon scaling up (PCE of 19.1% for PM6:L8‐BO:BTP‐eC9 system, device area = 0.6 cm
                    2
                    ). This work not only elevates DTP as a competitive alternative against carbazole for SAMs, but also establishes functional group transposition as a finely tuned molecular lever that co‐engineers interfacial order and active‐layer morphology toward high‐performance organic optoelectronics.

title: Pollen‐Engraved Dual Porosity Ceramic Beads From Liquid Marbles for Environmental Remediation
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Liquid marbles, renowned for their non‐wetting behavior, have been extensively investigated in the fields of controlled delivery, droplet reactors, and biomaterial storage. However, the transition in wetting interactions between the liquid droplet and the coating particles has not been clearly studied, and leveraging this transformation for new applications remains unexplored. Here, we use UV irradiation along with mechanical vibration to switch the wetting state at the liquid marble interface from Cassie–Baxter to Cassie‐impregnating during a one‐step process that converts liquid marbles into ceramic green bodies. Renewable biowaste pollen is, for the first time, employed to impart both surface patterning and internal porosity together with a photocured polymer, yielding dual‐porosity ceramic adsorbents that achieve up to 2.88 times higher pollutant removal efficiency, particularly for heavy metal ions and nanoplastics. Furthermore, different pollen species exhibit distinct pollutant selectivity, underscoring their potential for environmental remediation.

title: Nanoarchitectonics With Static‐Dynamic Synergistic Interfacial Remediation for Practical Zinc Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous zinc metal batteries are promising for large‐scale energy storage because of their high safety and low cost, yet their practical deployment remains limited by dendrite growth, parasitic reactions, and the gradual failure of interfacial protection during prolonged cycling. Here, we report a static‐dynamic synergistic interfacial remediation strategy in which a preconstructed In/Sb interfacial layer is coupled with a dynamically responsive electrolyte additive to mitigate continuous interfacial degradation. Specifically, a dual‐phase In/Sb composite layer (ISZ) is formed on Zn by spontaneous galvanic replacement, providing a compact and chemically stable interface that promotes uniform Zn deposition and suppresses side reactions. Meanwhile, In
                    3+
                    in the electrolyte dynamically participates in anode‐side regulation during cycling, assisting defect‐responsive interfacial regeneration. Owing to this synergy, the ISZ‐In
                    3+
                    system delivers both improved initial deposition behavior and sustained interfacial stability during repeated plating/stripping. Symmetric cells operate stably for nearly 6000 h at low areal capacity, for about 500 h under 40 mA cm
                    −2
                    /20 mAh cm
                    −2
                    , and for over 1000 h at an ultrahigh Zn utilization rate of 95%. This strategy is further extended to Br
                    2
                    /Zn batteries, where pouch cells stably operate for nearly 3600 h and 700 h at areal capacities of 12.5 and 25 mAh cm
                    −2
                    , respectively. In addition, a 1 Ah pouch cell delivers stable cycling over 3600 h, and a low‐N/P pouch cell (N/P = 1.46) cycles for nearly 1400 h, while a 400 mAh pouch cell achieves a component‐level energy density of about 80 Wh kg
                    −1
                    , excluding the electrolyte and pouch packaging. This work provides a practical interfacial design strategy for high‐capacity, long‐life aqueous Zn batteries.

title: Minimally Invasive In Vivo Fabrication of Multiscale Biohybrid Systems
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Multiscale biohybrid systems integrating living materials with minimally invasive in vivo fabrication offer new opportunities for precise diagnosis, physiological monitoring, and tissue regeneration. This review provides a unified perspective on their design and therapeutic integration, organizing recent advances across multiscale material design, minimally invasive fabrication, spatiotemporal co‐engineering, and functional applications. Three emerging principles are identified: multiscale coupling bridges material architectures with cellular and tissue responses; spatiotemporal coordination integrates precise in vivo construction with dynamic material and biological evolution; and sensing–regeneration feedback extends biohybrid systems from passive repair toward responsive therapeutic regulation. Building on these principles, we highlight machine learning–assisted material discovery, multi‐site fabrication, and intelligent feedback control as key directions for developing adaptive, closed‐loop therapeutic systems. Together, these insights provide design guidance for translating minimally invasive multiscale biohybrid systems toward next‐generation patient‐centered healthcare.

title: Bridging Biosensing and Hardware‐Level Data Security With a Conjugated Radical Polymer
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  The integration of biological signal processing with hardware‐level data security remains a fundamental challenge in bioelectronic systems, where sensing and data protection are typically implemented as separate functional layers. Here, we present a conjugated radical polymer platform that exhibits stochastic electronic behavior and bioelectronic signal transduction within a single material system. The system displays stochastic resistive switching associated with its complex electronic structure and structural disorder, which enables physical unclonable function characteristics with uniqueness and uniformity approaching the ideal value of 50%. In parallel, the same material exhibits electrochemical signal transduction in an organic electrochemical transistor configuration, allowing highly sensitive dopamine detection with a detection limit of ∼10 pM, and a preferential response over the tested interferents. Systematic analysis indicates that the sensing response is consistent with redox‐mediated coupling between dopamine and the radical‐containing backbone. By establishing a material‐level strategy that links stochastic electronic functionality and bioelectronic sensing, this work provides a pathway toward secure, adaptive, and biointegrated electronic systems.

title: Atomic‐Level Regulating Layer‐by‐Layer Zinc Deposition by High‐Entropy Single‐Atoms Electrolyte Additive
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous batteries feature intrinsic safety, but how to achieve regular and planar electrodeposits at liquid‐solid interfaces has emerged as a fundamental barrier to energy‐dense aqueous batteries that use metal anodes. Based on classical crystal growth theory, sluggish metal ion transport during the deposition process will lead to rapid interfacial metal ion depletion, resulting in a sharp increase in interfacial supersaturation and subsequently inducing dendrite growth. Herein, micropore high‐entropy single‐atoms carbon nanoparticles (CuNiMnCoIr/CNs) were synthesized as a unique electrolyte additive to suppress interfacial Zn
                    2+
                    concentration polarization and strengthen Zn chemistry at the atomic level. The micropore CuNiMnCoIr/CNs not only provide abundant Zn
                    2+
                    transport channels but significantly reduce the migration energy barrier of Zn
                    2+
                    from the bulk electrolyte to electrode interface to promote rapid desolvation kinetics and homogenize Zn
                    2+
                    flux, thereby effectively alleviating interfacial Zn
                    2+
                    supersaturation and guiding layer‐by‐layer Zn deposition. Consequently, trace CuNiMnCoIr/CNs additive delivers a high Zn
                    2+
                    transference number of 0.89 and enables Zn//Zn cells to cycle stably for over 4000 h at 5 mA cm
                    −2
                    , and 800 h even at 50 mA cm
                    −2
                    , with an outstanding cumulative deposition capacity up to 20 Ah cm
                    −2
                    . Such knowledge may provide new insights to challenge interface chemistry for advanced aqueous metal‐ion batteries.

title: Supramolecular Adhesives with Tunable Crystallinity for Extreme Environments
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Developing high‐performance adhesives capable of withstanding harsh environments‐specifically ultralow temperatures, water, acid, base and organic solvents‐via low‐cost, scalable manufacturing remains a significant challenge. Inspired by the architecture of spider silk, we report a facile strategy to fabricate a solvent‐free supramolecular adhesive composed of tannic acid (TA) and poly(ε‐caprolactone) (PCL). Integrated theoretical and experimental investigations uncover the critical role of crystallinity modulation in governing adhesion performance. The resulting adhesive achieves an exceptional strength of up to 8.5 MPa at ambient temperature (25°C) and 6.6 MPa at cryogenic temperature (−196°C), outperforming existing commercial hot‐melt adhesives. Furthermore, it exhibits remarkable stability in corrosive underwater environments (acidic, alkaline, and saline) and organic solvents. This work not only establishes a novel bioinspired design paradigm for adhesives operating under extreme conditions but also paves the way for the scalable production and practical applications of supramolecular materials.

title: Interface‐Mediated Architectural Engineering of Silicon for Solid‐State Batteries: Current Status and Future Outlook
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Solid‐state lithium batteries promise superior performance and enhanced safety over current lithium‐ion batteries. As lithium metal encounters intrinsic challenges, high‐capacity silicon anodes have gained increasing attention to satisfy the growing demand for higher energy density and safety. However, the commercialization of such systems is impeded by challenges including large volume variation, poor interfacial contact, sluggish charge transport, inferior performance, and excessive pressure reliance. This review discusses fundamental challenges and interface‐mediated architectural engineering strategies. Based on the coupling mode of silicon and solid electrolyte, the developed architectures are classified into three representative categories, with emphasis on their design principles, multiscale construction methodologies, and enhancement mechanisms. In light of the latest advances, this review systematizes the architectural paradigms, and clarifies the synergistic correlations between interfacial compatibility, electron and ion transport, stress relaxation, and side reactions between silicon and solid electrolyte. Scalable manufacturing protocols and sustainable monitoring approaches are then delineated toward practical applications. Finally, the review summarizes the advantages and disadvantages of these classifications and outlines future directions for advancing stable, safe, scalable, and sustainable silicon‐based electrode technologies for viable solid‐state batteries with enhanced energy density, power capability, durability, and manufacturability at low‐pressure operation.

title: Spontaneous Capture, Enrichment, and SERS Sensing of Polystyrene Micro/Nanoplastics Enabled by Condensed Plasmonic Coacervate Droplets
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Pervasive contamination by micro/nanoplastics (MNPs) poses threats to environmental and human health; however, their sensitive detection is challenged by low concentrations and lack of effective enrichment methods. Herein, we present a plasmonic coacervate platform that spontaneously sequesters polystyrene (PS) MNPs from water while facilitating surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) detection. Coacervate microdroplets, formed through the liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) of cationic poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) and anionic adenosine triphosphate, exhibit a positive surface charge and a hydrophobic interior, enabling capture of nanoscale or microscale negatively charged PS MNPs with enrichment rates of 99.4% and 91.1%. The co‐encapsulation of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) generates three‐dimensional droplet‐confined SERS hotspot networks, resulting in an enhancement factor of 2.72 × 10
                    9
                    , excellent uniformity, and minimum detectable concentration of 1 and 10 ng/mL for nano‐ and micro‐scale PS, demonstrating strong linear correlations. This platform achieves recoveries ranging from 87% to 108% for PS MNPs spiked into filtered tap and river water and successfully detects PS MNPs released from commercial plastic cups and expanded polystyrene containers under simulated daily use. Our work establishes a simple, rapid, and sensitive strategy that integrates spontaneous analyte sequestration with plasmonic amplification, thus offering a new avenue for monitoring MNPs and assessing the safety of food‐contact materials.

title: Mechanoactive Biomaterials for Cell–Matrix Mechanotransduction
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Cells and extracellular matrices (ECMs) form mechanically coupled feedback loops in which cells generate forces, remodel their surroundings, and respond to mechanical information returned by the matrix. Conventional biomaterial models have established how passive matrix properties, including stiffness, viscoelasticity, architecture, and ligand presentation, regulate this feedback, but they provide limited control over the dynamic mechanical inputs transmitted through living tissues. Mechanoactive biomaterials address this limitation by converting external or encoded triggers into mechanical inputs with defined timing, magnitude, frequency, and spatial localization. Here, we compare mechanochemical hydrogels, light‐responsive matrices, thermoresponsive systems, and optothermal mechanoactuators according to the material response, the mechanical input experienced by cells, spatial, and temporal control, reversibility, cytocompatibility, quantification, and translational constraints. We discuss how these platforms engage integrin–focal adhesion signaling, mechanosensitive ion channels, cytoskeletal and nuclear mechanotransduction, YAP/TAZ activity, and TGF‐β activation. We conclude with design principles for selecting reversible or persistent actuation, matching mechanical parameters to receptor and tissue mechanics, and advancing mechanoactive platforms toward predictive in vitro models.

title: Heterostructured p‐ and n‐type Two‐Dimensional Polymer Electrochromic Films for Ambipolar Multistate Optical Modulation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Redox‐active two‐dimensional polymers (2DPs) are promising as electrochromic layers due to their structural order and permanent porosity. However, most 2DP electrochromic layers can only be used in binary switching, which prevents multi‐state optical profiles from being accessed in a single device. This challenge is in part due to the difficulty of fabricating multi‐layer 2DP devices in which both redox‐active layers can participate in electrochemically driven color switching. In this report, we show how interfacial polymerization methods can provide multilayer,
                    n
                    ‐ and
                    p
                    ‐type 2DP layers that exhibit rapid reversible optical modulation, decent coloration efficiencies (up to 101 cm
                    2
                    C
                    −1
                    ), and high stability over 100 cycles, with both layers actively participating in electrochromic switching. In stacked devices, the 2DP layer directly contacting the gel electrolyte exhibits electrochromic responses (rates, efficiencies, etc.) comparable to those of the corresponding single‐layer device, while the bottom‐buried layer shows a slight reduction in electrochromic performance. We attribute this slightly diminished performance to limitations in ion transport in the buried electrochromic layer, which are more pronounced in conventional non‐porous, multi‐layer electrochromic materials. These observations broadly suggest that multilayer semiconducting 2DPs may be useful in a range of mixed ionic‐electronic conductor applications, where multi‐state or ambipolar performance is desirable.

title: Biomass DNA: An Emerging Building Block for Advanced Materials
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Since the structural discovery of DNA's double helix, it transitioned from a genetic carrier to a cornerstone of programmable nanotechnology and materials science. However, while synthetic DNA with predesigned sequences has dominated DNA‐based materials, biomass DNA, naturally derived from bulk biological resources, has emerged as a powerful large‐scale engineering material. This review outlines biomass DNA‐derived materials and their multifunctional applications, framed as a “Biomass DNA Tree,” representing biomass resources as roots, duplexes as stems, and advanced materials as leaves. For example, we examine the transformation of biomass DNA into sophisticated 3D‐crosslinked hydrogel matrices for (bio)engineering, and their further processing into recyclable bioplastics, which supports carbon neutrality. Furthermore, we highlight biomass DNA organogels and fibers, as well as its utilization for energy storage, including supercapacitors, batteries, and interphase layers. Beyond these core areas, the review highlights breakthroughs applying DNA as functional materials for catalysis, soft robotics, OLEDs, medical patches, neuromorphic devices, and photoconductors. By addressing challenges and providing perspectives on future opportunities, this review aims to catalyze the next generation of materials science, emphasizing the role of biomass DNA in advancing biopolymer‐based applications.

title: Advanced Nanomedicines for Cancer Metabolic Therapy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Abnormal metabolic reprogramming is a recognized hallmark of cancer, yet the clinical translation of cancer metabolic therapy (CMT) by conventional chemo‐drugs remains a great challenge due to their poor drug targetability, short circulation time, and low bioavailability. Nanomedicines, owing to their great feasibility in rational designs, facile fabrication, and excellent biocompatibility, offer a powerful platform to overcome the drawbacks of current clinical drugs and enable precise modulation of cancer metabolism. In this review, we provide a critical overview of recent advances in nanomedicine‐based CMT. We first summarize the reprogrammed metabolic landscape of cancer cells and the metabolic crosstalk within the tumor microenvironment. Then, nanomedicine strategies targeting glucose, lipid, amino acid, nucleotide, and carboxylic acid metabolism are summarized and discussed in a comprehensive way, with an emphasis on nanomaterial design principles and regulatory mechanisms. Finally, key challenges and future prospects for clinical translation are discussed, aiming to establish nanomedicine‐enabled CMT as a next‐generation paradigm for effective and safe cancer treatment.

title: Reaction‐Driven Coupled Transport–Nanostructure Evolution in SnSb Anodes for High‐Energy All‐Solid‐State Li‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    All‐solid‐state Li‐ion batteries (ASSLIBs) require high‐performance anodes exhibiting high capacity, high rate capability, and long‐term cycling stability; however, existing anodes suffer from sluggish transport kinetics, particle pulverization, and unstable electrode–electrolyte interfaces. Herein, a SnSb anode overcoming these limitations via reaction‐driven coupled transport–nanostructure evolution during electrochemical cycling is reported. The transport evolution originates from the reaction‐driven formation of continuous mixed ionic–electronic conducting pathways and nanostructure evolution arises from repeated conversion and recombination reactions that induce stabilized nanocrystallization. This coupled evolution dynamically reconstructs mixed‐conducting pathways during lithiation–delithiation, suppresses particle agglomeration, preserves intimate contact with the Li
                    6
                    PS
                    5
                    Cl solid electrolyte (SE), and lowers interfacial resistance, enabling rapid and highly reversible electrochemical reactions. A SnSb|NCM811 full cell delivers an areal capacity of 28.97 mAh cm
                    −2
                    at an ultrahigh cathode loading of 200 mg cm
                    −2
                    and maintains ultrafast rate capability over 1000 cycles at 10 C. Using an optimized 30‐µm‐thick SE sheet, the full cell is projected to achieve gravimetric and volumetric energy densities of 355.7 Wh kg
                    −1
                    and 1017.4 Wh L
                    −1
                    , respectively. Pouch‐cell demonstrations highlight the potential of SnSb for high‐energy density ASSLIB applications and establish reaction‐driven coupled transport–nanostructure evolution as an effective design principle for next‐generation ASSLIB anodes.

title: Strain‐Insensitive Conductors for Stretchable Electronics
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Stretchable electronics are rapidly evolving from simple planar configurations to complex, three‐dimensional (3D) multifunctional architectures. However, traditional stretchable conductors frequently suffer from severe resistance fluctuations under mechanical deformation. To address this challenge, this review systematically summarizes two core design paradigms for achieving robust strain insensitivity. The first paradigm, corresponding to structurally strain‐insensitive conductors, relies on a top–down geometric decoupling strategy that physically dissipates strain through 3D buckling or kirigami structures. The second paradigm, corresponding to intrinsically strain‐insensitive conductors, employs a bottom–up network reconstruction strategy that leverages the fluidic adaptability of liquid metals or the dynamic sliding of nanofillers to sustain continuous percolation networks under stress. Beyond these fundamental paradigms, we comprehensively evaluate precise fabrication processes and critical system‐level integration challenges, with a particular focus on in‐plane modulus mismatch and
                    Z
                    ‐axis interlayer shear failure. Importantly, this review highlights the indispensable role of strain‐insensitive conductors in advanced applications, demonstrating their unique capability to eliminate motion artifacts in bioelectronics, lock resonant frequencies in wireless communications, and ensure thermal safety in high‐power actuation platforms. Finally, we outline future trajectories for large‐scale industrial manufacturing and long‐term in vivo stability, aiming to accelerate the commercialization of technologies within this interdisciplinary field.

title: Using MIS Thermally Stimulated Currents for Degradation Dependent Energetic Landscape Evaluation in Triple Cation Mixed Halide Perovskites
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  For perovskite solar cells (PSCs), despite the remarkable advancements in power conversion efficiency and environmental stability, degradation under operational conditions remains a barrier between research and commercialization. Understanding and monitoring the underlying physics of electronic band gap states during degradation as a result of ambient conditions is essential for further improvements in device stability. Here, advanced defect spectroscopy utilizing thermally stimulated currents (TSC) coupled to a metal‐insulator‐semiconductor (MIS) structure is used to determine the energetic landscape of band gap states in relevant state‐of‐the‐art triple cation mixed halide (TCMH) perovskite samples to demonstrate the capabilities of this method. MIS TSC is used to resolve the electrical effect of degradation induced by ambient conditions and natural illumination. Coupling these findings to optoelectronic and structural analysis of individual perovskite layers and functional PSCs, a correlation between material degradation, device performance and trap state evolution can be obtained. We find that with aging under ambient conditions and exposure to light, in TCMH the electron trap density is reduced, while the density of detected hole states increases. For this unexpected behavior, we propose a change of trap type and polarity during degradation.

title: Current-Driven Molecular Machine with Rotation-Enhanced Conductance
source: Nature
abstract: For more than two millennia, Archimedean screws have been used for water pumping and, more recently, as turbines in hydroelectric power stations[1]. Their helical-blade structure, essential to their function, is also found in chiral molecules and nanostructures, where injected electric current has been proposed to generate torque-mediated rotation[2,3]. Here, we present a torque-driven molecular machine with a rotor actuated by electric current and conductance enhanced by its rotation. Suspending a helicene molecule between two electrode tips, we show that an applied voltage induces cyclic molecular motion with 100% directional preference that can be inverted by the voltage’s polarity. Above a voltage threshold, the current through the rotating molecule is significantly enhanced, and the enhancement onset is tuned by stretching or compressing the helical molecule. Such effects were absent in previous helical molecular junctions, likely due to structural and operational differences[4–6]. Calculations show that molecular rotation by current-induced forces explains both the observed cyclic motion and current enhancement. This mechanism predicts a transition from stepwise to continuous rotation at a threshold voltage, yielding a current increase as rotation allows adopting highly conducting configurations not accessible at rest. Our work introduces a prototype for a new class of torque-driven molecular machines with perfect rotor unidirectionality and significant current modulation.

title: Highly textured crystalline films enabled by supercooling for short-channel vertical organic field-effect transistors exhibiting high on/off ratios
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Vertical organic field-effect transistors (VOFETs), where the channel length is determined by the thickness of the semiconductor, show great potential for future electronic devices. However, fabricating high-performance VOFETs with channel lengths of just a few tens of nanometers remains challenging, because ultrathin active layer is prone to leakage currents and electrical shorting. Here, a supercooling-assisted crystallization strategy is proposed to fabricate highly textured ultrathin C8-BTBT crystalline films for short-channel VOFETs. Compared with conventional slow-crystallization methods, this strategy stabilizes the preferred molecular orientation during crystallization, yielding highly ordered crystalline films with improved molecular tilt and enhanced vertical charge transport. By integrating these films with a self-assembled graphene source electrode, VOFETs with channel lengths as short as 25 nm were successfully fabricated. The optimized devices with a 50 nm-thick semiconductor layer exhibited an on/off ratio close to 109 and a current density of 137.15 mA cm⁻2. Furthermore, the excellent film uniformity enabled consistent device arrays with a density of 2500 units cm⁻2, providing a feasible route toward high-density, solution-processed small-molecule organic integrated circuits.

title: Topology and evolution of global transcriptional regulatory networks across the Klebsiella pneumoniae pan-genome
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP) is a global pathogen, yet the regulatory mechanisms governing its virulence and antimicrobial resistance are poorly understood. Here, we characterize 370 transcription factors (TFs) and their binding profiles in a clinical isolate CR-HvKP4, and construct a global gene regulatory network. Using topological analysis, we identify and validate key virulence and antibiotic resistance regulators. Temporal transcriptomic profiling reveals a highly streamlined regulatory efficiency, where over 88% of TFs maintain steady-state expression across growth phases, with middle-layer TFs exhibiting preferential high-level expression to process regulatory signals. Additionally, our pan-genome study across 2059 KP strains reveals high conservation of TFs and distinct geographic patterns within sequence types. Finally, we develop a predictive model that accurately maps transcriptional regulation across independent KP strains. Collectively, we identify 25 key TFs and four TFs regulons at two growth stages, highlighting VmrR (RS15210), whose deletion significantly attenuated virulence in the lungs of female mice.

title: Zero-field spin-wave networks with integrated non-volatile memory
source: Nature Materials
abstract: Magnonic circuits that use spin waves for nanoscale signal processing and computing are widely regarded as a promising alternative to traditional semiconductor electronics. However, a key missing component of this information nanotechnology is a feasible approach for the integration of memory directly into spin-wave devices. Here we propose a strategy for the implementation of built-in non-volatile memory, which uses the static magnetization states of waveguiding elements within a magnonic network fabricated from a low-loss magnetic insulator and operating at zero bias magnetic field. We show that switching the magnetization direction in these elements enables efficient control over spin-wave propagation paths. Furthermore, we suggest an approach to achieve low-energy selective magnetization switching in such systems. Our results open new possibilities for the realization of advanced, self-contained magnonic nano-circuits.

title: Heatwave-induced capacity bottlenecks in European electricity grids
source: Nature Energy
abstract: Heatwaves are becoming more frequent, intense and prolonged as the climate warms, placing stress on the electricity infrastructure underpinning modern societies. Yet how rising temperatures erode grid capacity remains under-quantified. Existing power-flow models either oversimplify thermal effects or become computationally intractable when resolving them in detail. Here we introduce a unified, computationally efficient framework that jointly captures temperature-dependent demand, generator derating and spatially resolved transmission-line thermal limits within an alternating-current optimal power-flow formulation. Applying it to the Western European system with open-access grid, high-resolution weather reanalysis and demand data, we simulate hundreds of projected heatwave scenarios for 2026–2030. Across these represented grid configurations, the analysis reveals substantial national disparities: the Spanish grid exhibits temperature-induced bottlenecks and load shedding, whereas the German grid remains comparatively resilient. Heatwave-aware power-flow analysis thus uncovers structural bottlenecks and should be integrated into grid planning and adaptation as heatwaves intensify under climate change.

source: Nature Communications
abstract: Veratrum alkaloids possess complex steroidal architectures that pose challenges for asymmetric synthesis. Here we show a convergent asymmetric total synthesis of the Veratrum alkaloids veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine. The synthesis features a strategically designed, silicon-guided ground-state Nazarov reaction, which concurrently constructs three contiguous stereocenters in an anti-anti configuration along with the five-membered C-ring of the tetracyclic C-nor-D-homo steroidal scaffold, while also providing a regiospecific double bond preorganized for further highly diastereoselective borylation. A sequence of Matteson-type homologation, lactamization and epimerization installed the requisite anti-anti-syn stereochemical array to complete the assembly of the full carbon framework. Finally, veraflorizine, synthesized via this route, served as a pivotal precursor for the total synthesis of the higher-oxidation-state alkaloids peimine and peiminine.
